Agents.title: Claude Code Packs
Agents.intro: Beyond the hybrid workflow with Antigravity/Gemini, we package the memory, skills and native commands to use Claude Code on its own — the same rule base converted to <claudeMd></claudeMd> + <skillsDir></skillsDir> + <commandsDir></commandsDir>, following the <skillMd></skillMd> standard used by <skillsShLink></skillsShLink>. There's also a kit of <subagentsLink></subagentsLink> (<agentsDir></agentsDir>) ready to plug in.
Agents.stacksAvailable: {count, plural, one {# stack available} other {# stacks available}}

Subagentes.title: Subagents for Claude Code
Subagentes.intro: A kit of <agentsGlob></agentsGlob> that works in Claude Code alone or as a complement to a project already running the Gemini/Antigravity workflow — delegating specific tasks (code review, security auditing, debugging) to Claude Code without leaving the main flow. Each file runs in its own isolated context, with its own allowed tools, and is invoked by name or because its <description></description> matches the task.
Subagentes.whatIsTitle: What counts as a subagent here?
Subagentes.whatIsBody: An <md></md> file with frontmatter (<name></name>, <description></description>, <tools></tools>, <model></model>) in <agentsDir></agentsDir>. Claude Code delegates to it via the Task tool when the work matches its <description2></description2>, or when it's invoked explicitly by name. Unlike skills, it runs in its own context — it doesn't clutter the main conversation — and it can have restricted tools (e.g. a read-only auditor that can't use Edit).
Subagentes.listTitle: {count, plural, one {The agent in the kit} other {The # agents in the kit}}
Subagentes.downloadBody: The agents are the same for any stack — they're included by default in any Claude Code preset at <buildPath></buildPath>. You can also build the ZIP by hand and pick only the ones you want.

SkillCatalog.title: Skill Catalog
SkillCatalog.intro: Every skill in one place so you can decide what to install in the project at hand: what each one is for, when to use it, the exact install command and how it's invoked. Prefer them grouped by type of work (SEO, Web, Backend...)? <byProjectLink></byProjectLink>.
SkillCatalog.origins: The ones marked <hub></hub> already ship here and can be downloaded together from <buildLink></buildLink>. The <external></external> ones are third-party: installed separately, with their own command.

SkillsByProject.title: Skills by project type
SkillsByProject.intro: Skills combined by the kind of work you're doing — the same skill can show up in more than one category. Prefer them all together in a single table? <catalogLink></catalogLink>.
SkillsByProject.noInstallFallback: Included directly in the /build ZIP — no separate install needed.
